children: Democrats are discussing potential legislation to roll back President Trump's tariffs on Canada,
reported, citing the party's senior trade lawmaker in the Senate.
"There is overwhelming support for repealing the tariffs on products from Canada," said Sen. Ron Wyden (D-OR), ranking member of the Senate Finance Committee.
Wyden said he was already talking to colleagues about legislation to push back on the tariffs once he takes over the committee in January.

In a statement detailing Senate Finance Democrats' agenda, Wyden said he would use the "committee to reassert congressional authority over our country's trade policy to bring down costs, end Trump's disastrous and corrupt tariffs, reestablish critical trade partnerships, and hold trade cheats accountable."

Any measure to end the tariffs would require 60 Senate votes to override a filibuster. But overriding a presidential veto, which Trump has said he would use to block legislation when needed, would require 290 House votes and 67 Senate votes.
Democrats have so far captured 54 Senate seats and 253 House seats, meaning they would need to reach across the aisle for support.
Wyden and people close to him believe that the Canada tariffs are the best opportunity to flip Republicans against Trump,
reported. Notably, the tariffs were central campaign issues in border states like Michigan, Maine and Alaska.
"Ultimately, Congress must take away the president's ability to unilaterally and arbitrarily impose tariffs," Wyden said.

title: Democrats weigh measure to roll back Trump's Canada tariffs - report
